summary: The statement and proof are mathematically correct with the supplied predecessor and cited external theorem. The exact convex realization and mixed-area identities hold. The predecessor is correctly specialized to full planar metronoid mass, yielding the centroid bound for every containing closed ambient halfspace, including horizontal ones. Visual inspection of printed pages 60–61 of the primary Tsintsifas PDF confirms the alternating numerator sectors, opposite denominator sectors, and non-strict inequality used here: [Two inequalities for planar convex sets](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/DFDBE989B321D24672C69A1EFFCE0079/S0008439500007293a.pdf/two-inequalities-for-planar-convex-sets.pdf). The fan identities, selection argument, and triangle equality values are valid. The compact parameterization correctly handles the potential discontinuity from horizontal ambient normals; it proves continuity, boundary zero depth, interior positivity, and attainment on the middle fiber. The perturbation argument puts zero in the convex hull of active planar normals, and the antipodal-pair exclusion supplies the asserted positive fan. The retained-area estimates prove both retained sets have positive area before the self-contained planar Brunn–Minkowski argument is applied. All containments, strict inequalities, and square-root steps in the final contradiction have the stated directions, including the case s = delta/2. The integer-fiber extension correctly handles zero-area sections and consecutive positive sections. Finally, the explicit closed halfspaces verify the sharpness upper bound for every point in every fiber, and its limit establishes optimality. Boundary cases, equality cases, and the negation of the universal depth conclusion produce no counterexample or unresolved proof obligation.
